title-proc.eng: Laser for pump-probe spectroscopy at SLS 2.0

description-proc.fra: Il s'agit d'un appel d'offres pour un système laser qui sera utilisé au synchrotron Swiss Light Source (SLS2.0) pour des expériences de pompage-sondage sur deux lignes de lumière distinctes, SuperXAS et Phoenix. Ces expériences, menées dans le même bâtiment, nécessitent que le laser soit mobile entre les deux lignes de lumière. Pour la spectroscopie pompe-sonde, le laser doit fournir des longueurs d'onde réglables couvrant la gamme de l'ultraviolet (UV) au proche infrarouge (proche IR). La durée de l'impulsion laser doit être plus courte que celle des impulsions de rayons X, ce qui nécessite des impulsions de l'ordre de quelques dizaines de picosecondes (ps) ou moins. Une excitation efficace des matériaux étudiés nécessite un taux de répétition élevé compris entre 40 et 131 kHz, associé à une énergie d'impulsion élevée.
description-proc.deu: Dies ist eine Ausschreibung für ein Lasersystem, welches an der Synchrotron Lichtquelle Schweiz (SLS 2.0) für Pump-Probe-Experimente an den zwei Strahllinien SuperXAS und Phoenix eingesetzt werden soll. Da diese Experimente im selben Gebäude durchgeführt werden, muss der Laser zwischen den beiden Strahllinien mobil sein. Für die Pump-Probe-Spektroskopie muss der Laser abstimmbare Wellenlängen im Ultraviolettbereich (UV) bis zum nahen Infrarotbereich (nahes IR) liefern. Die Laserpulsdauer muss kürzer sein als die Röntgenpulse, sodass Pulse im Bereich von einigen zehn Pikosekunden (ps) oder kürzer erforderlich sind. Eine effiziente Anregung der untersuchten Materialien erfordert eine hohe Wiederholungsrate im Bereich von 40–131 kHz in Kombination mit einer hohen Pulsenergie.
description-proc.eng: This is a call for tender for a laser system which will be utilized at the Swiss Light Source 2.0 (SLS 2.0) synchrotron for pump-probe experiments at two distinct beamlines, SuperXAS and Phoenix. These experiments, conducted within the same building, require the laser to be mobile between the two beamlines. For pump-probe spectroscopy, the laser is to provide tunable wavelengths spanning the ultraviolet (UV) to near-infrared (near-IR) range. The laser pulse duration needs to be shorter than the X-ray pulses, thus requiring pulses in the tens of picoseconds (ps) or shorter timescale regime. Efficient excitation of the studied materials necessitates a high repetition rate in the range 40-131 kHz combined with a high pulse energy.

title-proc.eng: Expert support in the context of the State aid framework applicable to financial institutions

description-proc.eng: The subject of this call for tenders is expert consultancy services and reports in the context of the State aid framework applicable to financial institutions. Pursuant to article 108(3) TFEU, Member States have to notify State aid to the European Commission. The Member States can provide support to financial institutions in several ways. In case of unsound or failing credit institutions, Directive 2014/59/EU establishing a framework for the recovery and resolution of credit institutions and investment firms is applicable ("BRRD"- OJ L 173, 12.06.2014, p. 190). In case of impaired assets, the valuation has to be based on the Communication Paper on the Treatment of Impaired Assets in the Community Banking Sector (OJ C 72, 26.03.2009, p. 1). Member States can also provide support outside the BRRD in situations specified in the Communication from the Commission on the application of State aid rules to support measures in favour of banks (the 2013 "Banking Communication" - OJ C 216, 30.07.2013, p. 1). Lastly, Member States can provide support that is free of State aid that is in line with the Market Economy Operator Principles as summarised in Section 4.2 of the Commission Notice on the notion of State aid (OJ C 262, 19.07.2016, p. 1). The call for tenders is divided into three lots. Lot 1 will be used for the determination of whether a measure is in line with the Impaired Assets Communication, incorporating detailed asset valuations. Lot 2 will be used to obtain external support for determining whether a valuation that is conducted by another party is based on appropriate and consistent methodologies. Lot 3 will be used when expert support is needed for market conformity assessments in non-impaired asset measures, such as public guarantee measures, equity injections, or funding support. The Commission anticipates to utilize the expert support services on multiple occasions over the next few years. Although the broad scope of services may be described in advance, the timing, quantity or the specific focus of the needed services can only be known in the context of the specific case to be assessed within this period.

The contractor will be responsible for fine-tuning scenarios for sustainable transition of food systems, supporting the development of models for agroecological transition at both country and farm levels (including development of local modelers capacity), engaging stakeholders, disseminating and communicating project results, as well as providing management and coordination services. The stakeholder engagement will involve local organizations, including civil society, researchers, and policy makers, as well as regional organizations in Africa, to ensure a comprehensive and inclusive approach. A key dimension of the project is to engage with policy makers from the outset, to ensure a good understanding and uptake of the project's lessons and recommendations, and to facilitate the integration of the project's findings into policy decisions. This contract is necessary to support the project's objectives, which require specialized expertise and services to model sustainable food systems transitions, engage with stakeholders, and effectively manage and coordinate the project's activities, ultimately contributing to the Commission's goal of promoting sustainable agriculture and food systems in Africa.

title-proc.eng: 81322354-Promoting digital solutions in Technical and Vocational Education and training delivery in Benin

description-proc.eng: Benin has a young population of 13.4 million. With an annual demographic growth rate of 2.7?% (2022), 42?% of the population is under 15. Every year, around 200,000 young people join the labour market. Despite economic growth of around 6?% per year (2017-2022), the labour market is not in a position to offer qualified employment to all young people. 84?% of the workforce works in precarious conditions in the informal business sector. And 72?% of the workforce (92?% of young people aged 15 to 24) is underemployed in terms of income or working hours. The result is a high poverty rate of 49.6?% and a highly unequal distribution of income (Gini coefficient of 0.48) (World Bank 2022). The TVET system is not sufficiently capable of preparing young people for the labour market. The number of students registered in technical and vocational education and training (TVET) is low compared to the number of students in general secondary education. Currently, 30,000 young people, 31?% of whom are women, are enrolled in formal TVET, corresponding to 3.8?% of all secondary school students. The low enrolment in TVET can be explained by the lack of formal training opportunities of this type, the high entry requirements, the lack of information among families about the needs of the labour market, and the high fees for trainees" families. Recognising the constraints of the national TVET system, the government has adopted a National Strategy for TVET 2020 - 2030, which aims for higher quality of technical and vocational skills and qualifications in priority sectors of the country's economy. The government is also committed to enhance the governance of the system, the modernisation of curricula and the certification of apprenticeships. In this way, it aims to contribute to the structural transformation of the economy as reflected in the Government Action Programme PAG2 (2021-2024). The Federal Republic of Germany is supporting Benin in the operationalization of the reform of its vocational training system through, among other initiatives, the "Promotion of vocational training" Project (ProFoP). The project aims to improve the institutional framework for a formal vocational training offer aligned with the needs of the local economy. To this end, it encourages the establishment of systematic cooperative relationships between state structures in charge of vocational training and the private sector, as well as the piloting of cooperative training approaches in selected sectors. The project measures support practical, inclusive vocational training that meets the needs of the national economy. In this way, they contribute to increasing opportunities for decent employment and secure income, particularly for women. The module is structured around four main outputs: Output 1 aims to strengthen the steering and implementation capacities of public and private sector structures involved in the governance and coordination of vocational training. Output 2 aims to improve cooperation mechanisms between state and private-sector players in the field of dual vocational training. Output 3 is aimed at piloting dual vocational training provision in the selected sectors of renewable energies, agriculture, IT and other prospective sectors, which are relevant to the labour market. This means that parts of the training are carried out in a company. Output 4 aims to improve career guidance, training support and integration measures for young people, particularly women and disadvantaged groups.

title-proc.eng: Review of regulation of safety in election implementations.

description-proc.eng: The aim of the review is to contribute to increased knowledge on the degree to which the current regulations contribute to sufficient physical and digital security by holding elections in the municipalities and counties. The review shall give the ministry a better basis to assess whether there is a need to regulate some requirements that can contribute to strengthening the security of the municipalities' and counties' elections in more detail in the Election Act or the election regulations, as well as assess the need to strengthen or adjust the guidance in the area. The ministry believes it is important to avoid overlapping regulations or that similar regulations allow for interpretation issues. A central part of the assignment is therefore to map to what degree the existing regulations will apply to the municipalities' and counties ́ safety work connected to election implementation. Existing rules mean all laws and regulations that meet the municipalities, not just rules for election implementation. Today it is not possible to vote electronically in Norwegian elections. The Ministry would like an independent part of the assignment to be carried out an assessment of how any implementation of electronic voting will affect the safety picture and regulation of safety in the election implementation. The assignment is divided into two parts, with part 2 building on the results of part 1. Part 1 is the largest part of the assignment and means that the tenderer shall carry out a mapping of existing regulations and analyse how it can be facilitated for the best possible security and preparedness in the municipalities ́ election implementation. This shall provide the Ministry with a basis for investigating whether there are areas where there is a need to regulate security further or offer increased guidance. The estimated value of the procurement is up to NOK 1,500,000 excluding VAT. The estimated value is not binding for the contracting authority. title-proc.eng: Delivery of Conservation Measures with a focus on control of Rhododendron in Twelve Bens/Garraun Plateau SAC , Mweelrea/Sheeffry/Erriff Complex SAC Maumturk Mountains SAC and the Connemara Bog Complex

description-proc.eng: This Call for Tender seeks a contractor to implement works as part of a multi-actor, community embedded ecosystem restoration programme. Building on pilot projects, 2021 to 2025, in Galway, Mayo, and Donegal, the contractor will focus on delivering peatland restoration whilst also building local capacity to address threats to peatland habitats, including Rhododendron ponticum, within the Connemara/SW Mayo region. Constructive engagement with farmers and landowners is a crucial element of this contract. Scope of work and deliverables The successful contractor will be responsible for delivering the following core pillars, Stakeholder Engagement and Capacity Building: Lead extensive formal and informal engagement with landowners, local authorities, NPWS and ACRES CP teams. This includes informing and engaging landowners, managing expressions of interest, EOIs, for peatland restoration, collaborating on a training programme for restoration methods, and upskilling personnel including farmers in the implementation of restoration actions, as appropriate. Surveying and Mapping: Complete comprehensive mapping of threats, invasive species, drainage, bare peat, across 15 high-priority sub catchments by 30th September 2026, see Appendix. This data will inform Site Specific Conservation Objectives, SSCOs, and blanket bog Provisional Restoration Requirements PRRs. PRRs are a new NPWS approach to identifying and prioritising areas with the highest restoration potential. Invasive Species Management: Implement Rhododendron control across c.300ha and re-treatment of c.190ha across the Twelve Bens, Connemara Bog, Mweelrea,Sheeffry,Erriff, and Maumturk Mountains SACs see Appendix.Peatland Restoration Planning: In partnership with LIFE IP Wild Atlantic Nature, oversee the restoration of c.70ha of blanket bog in Connemara following a detailed Restoration Action Plan. A draft Restoration Action Plan will be available to the successful contractor. Furthermore, the contractor will engage a hydro-ecologist or other suitably qualified person to develop three site-specific restoration plans covering c.250ha of blanket bog. Replacement of Rhododendron hedgerow: Manage a pilot scheme to replace Rhododendron hedgerows with native species and establish monitoring protocols for soil recovery in cleared areas. Tenderers should price for approximately 450m of hedgerow replacement. Communication, dissemination and networking: The successful tenderer will share information and findings from the project and engage in knowledge exchange with relevant stakeholders including other Natura Communities projects, Local Authorities, NPWS, FarmUP EIP, and others. This Call for Tender invites proposals from qualified contractors to further develop a multi-actor, community-led ecosystem restoration project, which is building on successful preliminary projects across Donegal, Mayo, and Galway refer to Appendix 5. Building on the foundational work established between 2021 and 2025, this contract focuses on scaling local capacity to execute restoration actions, primarily targeting Rhododendron ponticum control and broader peatland restoration. All actions must align with Site Specific Conservation Objectives SSCOs and address identified environmental pressures within the target areas. The successful tenderer will be responsible for: Convening and facilitating a Project Steering Group comprising relevant stakeholders and technical advisors. Appointing a dedicated Project Coordinator to manage the development and implementation of the Conservation Measures programme. Providing comprehensive technical and administrative support, including specialist ecological advice on Rhododendron management, GIS mapping, and the provision of all necessary training materials and equipment. Maintaining continuous engagement with local landowners and community actors to ensure transparency and maximise participation.

The tender competition is restricted and it will be carried out in two stages. The relative point model is further described here: https://www.anskaffelser.no/verktoy/veiledere/veileder-i-evaluering-av-tilbud/poengmodeller#section-relativ-poengmodell-0 PROJECT OVERVIEW AND BACKGROUND INTRODUCTION Museum Nord shall engage a designer/design company to design and construct a new exhibition for the Lofotr Viking Museum at Borg, Lofoten. Museum Nord is a non-profit, government-backed organisation in the Norwegian national museum network, which operates 21 different museums in northern Nordland. Despite its location north of the Arctic Circle, Museum North is one of Norway's most visited museums. Our 21 facilities include major facilities such as the Lofotr Viking Museum and the Hurtigrute museum, as well as many smaller sites, such as village museums and cultural heritage centres of local importance. www.museumnord.no BACKGROUND The Lofotr Viking Museum in Vestvågøy is built on site for an extraordinary archaeological discovery - the longest viking longest ever found, a powerhouse and home for generations of chiefs. The site was discovered in 1981, and in 1994 a full-scale reconstruction of the long house was built next to the original, and the museum opened its doors to the public. Lofotr is a major tourist attraction that attracts around 140,000 visitors a year, most international tourists, but also Norwegian tourists. In addition to the long house itself, Lofotr offers a wide range of experiences, including a new built port area, blacksmith, boats, horses and a broad programme of events and activities. Our visitor centre contains an introduction exhibition and a film, last updated in 2011, and which is now being renewed. The reconstructed long house includes two rooms - the living room and the banquet hall - presented by costume-clad interpreters. The third room in the long house, the barn (the byre), is currently used as a multi-purpose room. The museum has recently entered into a partnership with the team that produces the animated film ViQueens, which will be launched in 2026. The film is inspired by the objects and the history of Lofotr, and the museum wants to incorporate the film's tale, characters and digital resources into its new interpretation in order to attract new and younger visitors. Museum North recognises that the current exhibition does not give visitors a sufficiently clear, engaging and emotional introduction to history before they enter the long house. We know that visitors often do not understand the key ideas and that there is a lack of variation in interpretation methods. We wish to challenge common myths about the Viking Age, reflect cultural and social diversity in the Viking Age, and connect the archaeological history presented in the exhibition and the immersive experience in the long house. Summarised, our overall goal is to create new educational content and new programmes on Lofotr to improve the understanding of the Viking Age in Borg and Lofoten, and enhance the visitor experience for both the local community and tourists. We will also use the collaboration with the ViQueens movie to deliver new exhibitions and programmes. www.lofotr.no EXTENT OF THE WORK Museum Nord is looking for a designer/design company to deliver a new exhibition for the visitor centre and an updated room in the long house barn. The aim of the assignment: To design and build a new exhibition that: ·        is a clear, engaging and emotional framework for understanding before the visit to the long house. ·        provides an updated view of the Viking age in Lofoten. ·        provides an overview of the history from the finds and the excavation at Borg. ·        challenges common myths about the Viking Age. ·        reflects cultural and social diversity in the Viking Age. ·        is available, including and many in approach and presentation methods.

title-proc.eng: User observations on usage of recommender systems to enable scaling of recommender systems experiments through automated and agentic means

description-proc.eng: Pursuant to article 27 DSA, providers of online platforms must clearly explain in their terms and conditions the main parameters used in their recommender systems, using plain and intelligible language. Moreover, they must explain options for users to modify or influence these main parameters. The main parameters that must be explained include (a) the most significant criteria used to determine suggested information, and (b) the reasons for the relative importance of these parameters. For platforms offering multiple options for recommender systems, they must provide a functionality allowing users to select and modify their preferred option at any time. Such a functionality should be directly and easily accessible from the section of the platform’s interface where the information is prioritized. In addition to the obligations established by article 27, providers of VLOPs and VLOSEs have an additional requirement: they must provide at least one recommender system option that is not based on profiling as defined in Regulation (EU) 2016/679 (“General Data Protection Regulation” or “GDPR”). These transparency requirements aim to give users more control and understanding of how information is presented to them on online platforms, particularly in relation to personalized recommendations. Against this background, this contract will explore how users engage with recommender systems across Very Large Online Platforms (VLOPs) and Very Large Online Search Engine (VLOSEs) through user surveys and user observations. DG CONNECT, together with the European Centre for Algorithmic Transparency at the Joint Research Centre (ECAT – JRC), is developing new methods to analyze recommender systems. These methods are developed across a wide range of representative recommendation surfaces across VLOPs and VLOSEs (both in terms of user experience – social media feeds, products listing, etc. - and types of contents – video, text, images, products, etc.). Therefore, the need arises to ground the understanding of such systems with real world data from observations of user interactions with recommender systems, confronting state of the art of the scientific literature with the reality of a representative panel of VLOPs and VLOSEs’ user base (in terms of relevant demographic variables such as age, gender, computer literacy, etc.).
